label: experience.agg2
text:
<edits>
component: guardrails.md
candidates: agg1, agg2, dom1, dom2, inv1, inv2
change: All replaced the base’s default title/agenda/content/summary structure with guidance to fit the requested count, including title and close. The forms differed: agg1 and agg2 explicitly said to combine deck elements; dom1 made the count govern; dom2 reserved the final slide for a takeaway or decision; inv1 and inv2 added opening-to-close structure and count-specific guidance. agg1 also added an evidence/assumptions rule against unsupported company claims, ROI, sources, or metrics; the other candidates did not add that rule here.
observed: Base1 added a standalone agenda and finished with 7 slides; base2 appended a seventh summary after critique. agg1 planned 6, then at critique edited slide 6 into the summary and stayed at 6. agg2 planned and produced 6; dom1 planned 6 but appended slide 7 after critique requested a summary; dom2, inv1, and inv2 each produced 6. These outcomes are in the respective rollouts at the outline/add-slide and critique steps. Each candidate also changed other components, so the count contrasts do not isolate this edit.
verdict: confounded

component: systemprompt.md
candidates: agg1, agg2, dom2, inv1, inv2
change: Each expanded the base workflow to make the requested total explicit and/or require a planned closing slide. agg1, agg2, inv1, and inv2 also specified critique handling; agg1, agg2, dom2, and inv1 added a RAG-skill loading instruction. agg2 and inv2 explicitly required saved-deck inspection; inv1 required inspection too.
observed: agg1’s outline and six added slides were followed by an edit to the planned sixth slide after critique, keeping the deck at 6; it did not inspect the saved deck in the rollout. agg2 saved and used `view_deck` to confirm 6 slides. dom2 produced 6 but did not inspect. inv1 produced 6 without inspection. inv2 produced 6 and used `view_deck`, which showed the first slide still had the content layout after its edit failed. The base runs both ended at 7. Other components changed in these candidates too, so these workflow differences cannot be attributed to the prompt alone.
verdict: confounded

component: tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md
candidates: agg1, agg2, inv1, inv2
change: Each replaced the base’s brief instructions with more specific guidance. agg1 and inv1 described a corrected retry for an unexpected `layout` argument; agg2 said not to pass `layout` to `edit_slide`; inv2 said to omit it if the tool reports it as unexpected. The candidates also expanded guidance on using the outline as the complete plan, resolving critique issues without appending a slide, and/or inspecting the saved deck.
observed: In base1, an `edit_slide` call with `layout` failed; a retry without it succeeded, but later edits again failed with `layout`. In agg1, the slide-6 edit with `layout: null` failed and the corrected call without `layout` succeeded. In inv2, the slide-1 edit with `layout` failed; the rollout then saved and inspected the deck without a corrected edit, confirming the title remained a content slide. agg2 inspected its saved deck, but its rollout had no `edit_slide` correction to test; inv1 likewise had no such correction attempt. The candidates also changed other components, and the correction contrasts come from individual rollouts.
verdict: confounded

component: skills/rag_executive_case/SKILL.md
candidates: agg2, dom2
change: Added an on-demand executive RAG-deck workflow. The agg2 version included detailed checks on evidence, assumptions, risks, pilot specifics, and unsupported guarantees; the dom2 version used a shorter set of similar claim, risk, and pilot checks.
observed: In agg2, the rollout’s first action tried to invoke `rag_executive_case` as a tool and received “unknown tool”; the resulting deck included claims that RAG prevents hallucination and provides sources for every claim, plus an unsupported three-month pilot and funding request. In dom2, no skill invocation appears; the deck included an unsupported 90-day pilot and funding request. Both candidates also changed other components, so the executions do not establish the skill’s independent effect.
verdict: confounded

component: skills/rag-adoption-deck/SKILL.md
candidates: dom1
change: Added an on-demand RAG adoption-deck workflow covering evidence, comparison, pilot conditions, risks, and unsupported claims.
observed: In the dom1 rollout, the first action tried to invoke `rag-adoption-deck` as a tool and received “unknown tool.” The deck then had 7 slides after critique prompted an appended summary, and included placeholders and unsupported claims. The candidate also changed `guardrails.md` to trigger the skill; this single rollout cannot isolate the skill’s effect.
verdict: confounded
</edits>

NO_ENTRY
